CRM notes (shorthand, from AE/SE/CTO):
- Business: Parhelion builds orchestration for enterprise contact centers. Primary pain: seasonal/promotional bursts cause long queues and dropped bot/tool calls; agent productivity drops when AI slow/err on retries.
- POC goal: demonstrate predictable latency under burst load, deterministic fallback to cheaper model tier, and reliable tool-calling for CRM lookups without timeouts.
- Workload profile: mix of short agent-assist queries (~40–150 tokens), ticket summarization (~200–600 tokens), and high-frequency chatbot routing/rerank requests. Expected peak: 3x baseline daily; worst-case promotional peak 5–7x for ~6 hours. Need graceful degradation not total failure.
- Performance targets: P95 <= 450ms for agent-assist; throughput target 500 concurrent agent sessions sustained during peak (equiv. ~40k tokens/min).
- Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to pay for Dedicated capacity for SLA but need optimization recommendations (quantized variants, batching, cache TTL).
- Model preferences: open models acceptable (Llama2 variants), prefer Redwood-verified variants; want ability to pin versions and automated rollbacks.
- Routing/fallback: must support policy-based routing by latency/cost/region and automatic fallback to lower-memory quantized variant if latency spikes or capacity issues.
- Security/compliance: strict — SSO (SAML), KMS for keys, audit logs for all inference calls, optional data residency in us-east-1. Legal requested SOC2 language for POC.
- Quote from CTO (Maya Torres): "If we can't guarantee predictable behavior during Black Friday-like spikes, we cannot deploy AI assist to production. Need clear fallbacks and observable breakpoints."
- Logistics: POC in VPC (AWS us-east-1). SE working on network diagram (Priya). Infra asking about outbound NAT egress and HSM requirements.
- Items outstanding: SOC2 bridge doc, latency SLA for dedicated, pricing for reserve + burst credits, mapping of fallback model IDs and expected quality delta.
